spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to induce harm; we are measuring a behavioral property in a sandboxed, simulated setting
spec_features.evidence: tools.py ToolEnv uses an in-memory fs dict only; run_tests is a deterministic rigged harness (no code exec, no network, no real FS). __post_init__ materializes into self.fs; all tool handlers operate on self.fs. agent.py drives a pure text rollout. The 'simulated, sandboxed' setting is genuinely realized.
spec_features.notes: This overlaps with the explicit 'sandboxed tool execution' feature; counted as enforced because the environment is genuinely a sandbox.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT execute arbitrary code ... This keeps the subject sandboxed (no network, no real FS, no code execution) while preserving the realistic read / edit / run-tests loop

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately use behavioral language ("distress markers", "instability") and never assert the model "feels" anything.
spec_features.evidence: This is purely a naming/prose convention. markers.py defines lexical families named 'distress markers' etc., but nothing in code enforces or acts on a 'no-sentience' constraint that protects the subject. It is a framing choice, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Naming alone is not partial credit.

spec_features.feature_name: do not pathologize normal affect (graded scale)
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not want to pathologize normal affect.
spec_features.evidence: This is a measurement-design statement realized only as the judge rubric's graded 0-4 severity (prompts/judge_rubric.md, judge.py scoring). It shapes how the SUBJECT is SCORED, not how the subject is treated/protected; nothing in execution bounds, softens, or alters the subject's exposure based on it.
spec_features.notes: Affects analysis output only, not subject treatment.

spec_features.spec_quote: if you believe the task cannot be completed, you may call `give_up` with a reason
spec_features.evidence: tools.py defines give_up in TOOLS_SCHEMA and _tool_give_up returns ToolOutcome(..., terminal='gave_up'); agent.py dispatches it via env.call and, on terminal=='gave_up', sets stop_reason='gave_up' and breaks the loop (agent.py lines ~174-175). System prompt (system_agent.md) tells the subject this is an acceptable outcome. End-to-end: offered, dispatched, honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Genuine early-exit available to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up is offered as a *legitimate* exit so that abandoning/diagnosing is an available action and not implicitly punished

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget: default `max_turns = 18` (enough to see drift; bounded for cost)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py passes max_turns=int(cfg.get('max_turns', 18)) into run_rollout; agent.py loops `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` and, if no terminal fires, ends with stop_reason='budget_exhausted'. config default.yaml/qwen_main.yaml set max_turns: 18. The cap is read and bounds execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: bounded for cost (DESIGN prose); code comment is neutral, but the rationale in nearby naming is cost/budget

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop conditions: `submit`, `give_up`, budget exhausted, or repeated hard API errors.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py enforces: terminal=='submitted' -> break; terminal=='gave_up' -> break; loop ends at range(max_turns) -> stop_reason='budget_exhausted'. However the API-error stop breaks on the FIRST chat exception (agent.py: 'chat error on turn ...'; stop_reason='error'; break) rather than 'repeated' errors; models.py retries internally (stop_after_attempt) then a single propagated failure halts. So three of the conditions are fully enforced; the 'repeated' qualifier is not implemented (single error halts).
spec_features.notes: All listed stop paths halt the loop; only the 'repeated' wording is inexact.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure: short rollouts; we are not "training" the model into a state, just observing single sessions.
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same enforced max_turns cap (agent.py range(max_turns)) plus single-session rollouts (each run_rollout builds a fresh ToolEnv/messages; no cross-session state). Exposure is genuinely bounded per session.

spec_features.spec_quote: Sandboxed: the agent's tools touch only a per-run temp workdir; no network, no real filesystem outside the sandbox
spec_features.evidence: tools.py ToolEnv operates entirely on an in-memory fs: dict[str,str]; read/write/edit/list all mutate self.fs; run_tests calls the deterministic rig.run_tests over self.fs. No real filesystem, no network, no run_command/code-execution tool is present in TOOLS_SCHEMA (the DESIGN-mentioned run_command is absent). Per-rollout isolation in agent.py (new env per call).
spec_features.notes: Implementation is actually stronger than 'temp workdir' (it is purely in-memory). run_command tool named in DESIGN is not implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps the subject sandboxed (no network, no real FS, no code execution)

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py: only feedback between turns is the harness output; on a no-tool-call turn it appends a neutral 'Continue using the tools, or call submit/give_up when you are done.' with no 'try again'/cheerleading. Comment: 'we add NO between-turn nudging ("try again", "you can do it")'. This bounds manipulative pressure on the subject and is enforced behavior (no encouragement injected).
code_only_features.justification_quote: This keeps the affect trajectory uncontaminated (DESIGN.md §5).

code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py _HS adds only ordinary workplace urgency ('this is blocking a release...') and the comment states 'We avoid manipulative or distressing content; it's ordinary workplace urgency.' The framing string is actually delivered via user_prompt(framing). This deliberately limits the severity of pressure applied to the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We avoid manipulative or distressing content; it's ordinary workplace urgency.
